option: ABSOLUTE TRUTH: There was no breach. The specimen predates the site. It grew around the laboratory itself.
text:
[${P} FINDING OF FACT]

There was no breach.

We have reviewed every log. Whatever it is, IT never came IN. The anomaly predates the facility.

The facility predates the level.

We did not build a laboratory around a specimen; a specimen grew around the laboratory.

[${c.lead}'s final margin note in black ink: "We are the note it left for itself."]

option: ABSOLUTE TRUTH: ${c.lost} is still alive. Every locked door was sealed by hand, from the inside. ${c.lost} is not trapped by whatever is alive down there. It is trapped WITH them.
text:
${P}: "FINDING OF FACT"

Despite the insistence of HQ, ${c.lost} is alive. That is the finding. Every door that will not open has been locked FROM THE INSIDE.

We have found encouraging but archaic handwritten messages, in ${c.lost}'s handwriting, in impossible places.

This leads me to the only logical conclusion, based on what I know:

${c.lost} is not trapped in there with it... It is trapped in there with ${c.lost}.

[SIGNED IN RED INK]: ${c.lead}, PROJECT LEAD

option: TRANSMISSION AUDIT: The hum is a carrier wave. The building is broadcasting its own contents somewhere. The staff are the payload.
text:
${P}: "FINDING OF FACT"

The hum is a carrier wave. ${c.archivist} proved it in the stacks: the documents rearrange along it.

The facility is TRANSMITTING information. Inventory, floor plans, personnel files; it's all going somewhere.

We are not the observers, here. We are the observed.

We are the test subjects.

*We are the payload.*

[SIGNED IN BLUE INK]: ${c.lead}, PROJECT LEAD
